title: A standard projective-bundle fibre with its normalized line
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E a quasi-coherent finite locally free module of rank r>=2 [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], D a normalized tautological quotient for its canonical symmetric relative Proj [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], and s a point of S. Write p:P(E)->S and i_s:p.fiber(s)->P(E) for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There is an isomorphism e from standard projective space with r homogeneous coordinates over Spec kappa(s) to p.fiber(s), such that e^* i_s^* D.line is isomorphic to the standard O(1) [def-pc-projective-space-twist], using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. This asserts no classification of arbitrary invertible modules and no comparison of higher powers.

source.place: Tags 01OA and 01OE, section-projective-bundle and example-projective-space; lemma-relative-proj-base-change, Tag 01O3.

proof.text: Put X=Spec kappa(s), g:X->S and F=g*E, using tensor pullback. Compare tensor pullback with ordinary module pullback through their adjunctions. The proved source-library isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback instance and invariance under isomorphisms give F rank r. Choose a member of its finite-locally-free trivializing cover containing the unique point of X. Since X is nonempty and subsingleton, that member is top; isoFreeOfRestrictIso gives a global ordered free presentation. Write r=n+1, possible since r>=2. This step is proved in Lean, including the one-point trivialization helper.

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change (including its twist comparison); Tags 01OB and 01OE, definition-projective-bundle and example-projective-space.

proof.text: Use normalized descent to obtain a normalized quotient Dprime for F. Obtain generator-preserving symmetric-algebra pullback data b along g. Its relative-Proj base-change isomorphism q identifies P(F) with the scheme-theoretic fibre. The fixed-comparison quotient theorem applied to the given D and Dprime gives w:b.relProjComparison*D.line isomorphic to Dprime.line. The projection identity q.hom followed by fiber inclusion = b.relProjComparison identifies this with the pulled fibre line. No new quotient is substituted for the given D.

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change (including its twist comparison); Tags 01OB and 01OE, definition-projective-bundle and example-projective-space.

proof.text: Apply free_compatibility_of_normalized_quotient to Dprime and the inverse ordered free presentation. It gives eStd:P(F) isomorphic to standard projective space over X, and t:eStd*O(1) isomorphic to Dprime.line. Set e=eStd inverse followed by q. Pull w back along eStd inverse. Compose with the inverse transport of t, using tensor-pullback composition, eStd inverse followed by eStd hom = id, and tensor-pullback identity. These explicit isomorphisms prove the stated twice-pulled line comparison. This step and the inverse-pullback transport helper are complete Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_projective_bundle_fiber_twist_model (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (D : TautologicalQuotient E) (s : S) :
    ∃ e : ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin r); Spec (.of (S.residueField s))) ≅
        (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiber s,
      Nonempty
        ((tensorPullback e.hom).obj
          ((tensorPullback
            ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj D.line) ≅
          ProjectiveSpace.twist (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (Spec (.of (S.residueField s))) 1)
